case_name: Sussex County Planning & Zoning Commission v. Smokey Hollow, LLC

issues.label: Certiorari scope and record
issues.why: The court must define the permissible scope of review on certiorari and what parts of the Commission record it may consider.

issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must confirm it has jurisdiction to review the Commission action via certiorari despite any statutory appeal routes.

issues.label: Finality of Commission action
issues.why: The court must determine whether the challenged conditions constitute final, reviewable action.

issues.label: Exhaustion of administrative remedies
issues.why: The court must decide whether Smokey Hollow had to appeal to County Council or pursue reconsideration before seeking certiorari.

issues.label: Timeliness of petition
issues.why: The court must ensure the certiorari petition was filed within any applicable limitations period for judicial review.

issues.label: Standing of Smokey Hollow
issues.why: The court must confirm the developer is aggrieved by the conditions and has standing to seek relief.

issues.label: Proper parties and caption
issues.why: The court must ensure the correct governmental entity and officials are named for certiorari relief.

issues.label: Standard of review articulation
issues.why: The court must apply the correct mix of de novo review for legal issues and substantial-evidence review for factual findings/discretion.

issues.label: Presumption of administrative regularity
issues.why: The court must decide what deference, if any, is owed to the Commission’s interpretation and application of its code.

issues.label: Commission statutory authority
issues.why: The court must determine the extent of the Commission’s delegated authority under Title 9 and the County Code.

issues.label: Commission code-based authority
issues.why: The court must interpret Chapter 99/115 provisions authorizing conditional approval and what limits they impose.

issues.label: Mandatory approval if compliant
issues.why: The court must resolve whether compliance with the Code requires approval absent reasonable mitigating conditions.

issues.label: Conditioning power limits
issues.why: The court must define whether conditions may exceed code minima or must be tethered to explicit standards.

issues.label: Reasonableness test content
issues.why: The court must identify the correct legal standard for when a subdivision condition is “reasonable” and not arbitrary.

issues.label: Nexus to legitimate interests
issues.why: The court must decide whether each condition bears a rational nexus to health, safety, welfare, drainage, wetlands, and impacts.

issues.label: Rough proportionality
issues.why: The court must assess whether the severity of each condition is proportionate to the projected impacts it addresses.

issues.label: Findings and explanation duty
issues.why: The court must determine whether the Commission must articulate reasons and factual findings for each contested condition.

issues.label: Substantial evidence support
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the record contains substantial evidence for flooding/wetland/access findings supporting Condition A.

issues.label: Reliance on public testimony
issues.why: The court must decide how much weight lay public testimony can carry versus technical evidence in imposing conditions.

issues.label: Impermissible political opposition
issues.why: The court must assess whether conditions were imposed to appease neighborhood opposition rather than to mitigate demonstrable impacts.

issues.label: Consistency with County Code text
issues.why: The court must interpret relevant code provisions to see if Conditions A and O conflict with the enacted standards.

issues.label: Setback vs buffer distinction
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Code regulated only building setbacks (25 feet) or also authorized a fixed wetland buffer.

issues.label: Authority to eliminate a lot
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Commission may require deletion of a conforming lot as a condition of subdivision approval.

issues.label: Access across wetlands legality
issues.why: The court must assess whether lot access requiring wetland crossing is prohibited or triggers enforceable design constraints.

issues.label: Wetlands delineation evidence
issues.why: The court must determine whether wetland boundaries/encroachment were established by competent evidence in the record.

issues.label: Flooding and drainage impacts
issues.why: The court must decide whether predicted flooding/runoff impacts are supported and whether deletion is necessary to mitigate them.

issues.label: Alternative mitigation consideration
issues.why: The court must consider whether the Commission was required to evaluate less restrictive alternatives (e.g., buffers, easements, design changes).

issues.label: Condition A code conflict claim
issues.why: The court must resolve whether Condition A conflicts with legislative judgments such as subdivision perimeter setback requirements.

issues.label: Buffer requirement authority
issues.why: The court must determine whether any code provision empowered the Commission to impose a 25-foot fixed wetland buffer.

issues.label: Condition O explanation adequacy
issues.why: The court must decide whether imposing Condition O without an articulated rationale is legal error or arbitrary action.

issues.label: Ordinance 2852 applicability
issues.why: The court must interpret whether the later ordinance applies to this application and what “pending applications” exemption means.

issues.label: Retroactivity and vested rights
issues.why: The court must decide whether Smokey Hollow had vested rights under the prior code and whether new buffer rules can apply.

issues.label: PLUS review legal effect
issues.why: The court must assess whether completion of PLUS review constrains County conditions or affects vested rights expectations.

issues.label: Coastal Area requirements
issues.why: The court must determine whether Coastal Area status or any environmental assessment requirements affect wetland-buffer authority.

issues.label: Cluster standards applicability
issues.why: The court must decide whether cluster development standards could legally be invoked to justify Condition O.

issues.label: Interpretation of key definitions
issues.why: The court must interpret definitions of “building setback,” “resource buffer,” and “not subdividable” and their legal consequences.

issues.label: Preemption by state wetlands law
issues.why: The court must consider whether state or federal wetlands regulation preempts or limits County-imposed wetland conditions.

issues.label: Takings and exactions concerns
issues.why: The court must consider whether deleting a lot or imposing buffers constitutes an unconstitutional taking or unlawful exaction.

issues.label: Procedural due process
issues.why: The court must ensure the developer received fair notice and an opportunity to be heard regarding the bases for the conditions.

issues.label: Equal protection / uniformity
issues.why: The court must consider whether imposing conditions beyond code standards treats this applicant differently without a rational basis.

issues.label: Consistency with comprehensive plan
issues.why: The court must decide whether the subdivision (and conditions) must be consistent with the County Comprehensive Plan and how.

issues.label: Adequate record for review
issues.why: The court must determine whether the Commission created an adequate record (minutes, exhibits, findings) to permit judicial review.

issues.label: Scope of remedy on certiorari
issues.why: The court must decide whether it may strike conditions outright, remand for findings, or require reconsideration under correct standards.

issues.label: Severability of conditions
issues.why: The court must determine whether removing Conditions A and O affects the validity of the remaining approval/conditions.

issues.label: Harmless error analysis
issues.why: The court must assess whether any procedural or explanatory deficiency was prejudicial or harmless given the record.

issues.label: Burden of proof allocation
issues.why: The court must decide who bears the burden to show unreasonableness/illegality versus support in the record.

issues.label: Commission vs Council roles
issues.why: The court must delineate the Commission’s administrative role versus County Council’s legislative role in setting development standards.

issues.label: Appellate precedent application
issues.why: The court must apply controlling Delaware precedent on subdivision approvals and reasonable conditions to these specific facts.
